message.content: In domestic cats and many other felids, the presence of a mane in male lions is governed by a **dominant allele**. In lions, the gene that controls mane development (often linked to the *MC1R* or *ASIP* loci) is expressed when at least one copy of the dominant allele is present. Thus, a male lion inherits a mane if he carries the dominant allele for mane growth, regardless of the allele inherited from his mother. This dominant trait is one of the most striking phenotypic features that distinguishes male lions from females.
